history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed (Buddhist monastery, Nyingma order). A more than 300-year-old gompa on a ridge near Kaluk/Rinchenpong, one of the oldest surviving structures in the area; 'Reesum' is explained locally as 'three ridges', the point where three ridges meet. An old stupa wall with mani stones marks the former gateway. Until the early 20th century it was a site of tantric sadhana, where Buddhist yogis from across Sikkim undertook long meditation under the locally renowned Reesum Rinpoche, who dug a sacred pond to water the ridge. A traditional three-year, three-month retreat is still practised in a closed compound behind the monastery. The monastery is built of wood: whitewashed packed-earth walls with a two-tiered wooden pagoda roof, latticed entrance and wooden prayer wheels. Specific deities, founding lama and exact founding year are undocumented — flagged. Coordinates from map geocoding near Rinchenpong are approximate — flagged (verify). name: Reesum Monastery
town_description: Rinchenpong is a hill town in West Sikkim at about 1,700 m, near Kaluk, about 123 km west of Gangtok. It is known for its monasteries, trekking routes, the historic Poison Pokhri (Bikh Pokhri) lake, and panoramic views of Mt. Kangchenjunga.

travel.airport: Nearest airport: Bagdogra (IXB), about 130–135 km (4–5 hrs by road). Pakyong Airport is closer (~105 km) but flights are infrequent.
travel.road: Forest trail from Kaluk village near Rinchenpong; about 3–4 hrs by road from Gangtok, 5 hrs from Siliguri.

visitor_information.best_time: October–May (dry season; winter offers the clearest Kangchenjunga views).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published (verify); the retreat compound behind the monastery is closed to visitors.
